body_md: Profile with `cargo flamegraph`: samples stacks into SVG. Run on release binary. Wide bars are hot paths. Fix allocation and cloning first — they dominate.
code:
$ cargo install flamegraph
$ cargo flamegraph --bin app
# open flamegraph.svg
hook: Find the 5% of code eating 95% of time — flamegraph shows it.

quiz.explain: Flamegraph visualizes sampled stacks; width is time share.

trap: Profiling debug builds misleads; always release + debuginfo.

body_md: `perf stat` counts cycles, cache-misses, branch-misses. `perf record/report` pinpoints symbols. High miss rates mean layout or branch fixes, not micro-tweaks.
code:
$ perf stat ./target/release/app
$ perf record ./target/release/app
$ perf report
hook: Cache misses cost 100x — perf counts what profilers hide.

quiz.explain: perf reads hardware counters for true bottlenecks.
quiz.q: How do you measure cache misses?

trap: Tuning without counters optimizes wrong function.

body_md: Swap allocators for throughput: `#[global_allocator] static A: tikv_jemallocator::Jemalloc;` or mimalloc. Gains 10-30% on alloc-heavy servers. Measure with benches.
hook: One line, 20% faster server — swap the allocator.

quiz.q: How do you switch to mimalloc?

takeaway: Allocator choice matters for alloc-heavy apps.
trap: Jemalloc static bloat on tiny binaries; measure binary size.

body_md: SIMD processes 4-8 lanes at once. `std::simd` (nightly) or `wide` crate auto-vectorizes loops. Check with `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native"` for AVX gains.
hook: Do 8 adds in one instruction — SIMD is free speed.

quiz.explain: SIMD executes one op across multiple lanes.

trap: Unaligned loads or branches kill vectorization silently.

body_md: `#![no_std]` drops std for embedded: use `core` + `alloc`. No threads, no files. Add panic handler, `cortex-m-rt` target. Allocations via `heapless` fixed buffers.
hook: Rust on a $2 chip with no OS — no_std makes it possible.

quiz.explain: no_std removes OS dependency, keeps core.
quiz.q: How do you run Rust bare-metal?

trap: Using std types (File, Thread) in no_std fails to compile.

body_md: Cut allocations: reuse buffers with `clear()`, `String::with_capacity`, `BytesMut` pools. Clone in loop is top perf killer — borrow or `Cow` instead.
hook: The fastest allocation is the one you never do.

quiz.q: How do you cut allocator pressure?

trap: String::new in loop reallocs every iteration.

body_md: Release tuning: `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true` in Cargo.toml. PGO via `RUSTFLAGS="-Cprofile-generate"` adds 10-20%.
hook: Three lines in Cargo.toml shrink and speed your binary.

quiz.explain: LTO inlines across crates for speed/size.
quiz.q: Best release profile for max speed?

takeaway: Tune release profile for size and speed.
trap: LTO slows builds 3x; gate behind release pipeline.

body_md: Zero-copy parsing with `&str` slices, `bytes::Bytes` refcounted views, `serde` borrowed `&'a str`. Avoid `to_string` in parsers — slice the input instead.
hook: Parse gigabytes without copying a byte — zero-copy.

quiz.explain: Borrowed slices reference input without copy.
quiz.q: How do you parse without allocations?

takeaway: Slice inputs; avoid owned copies in parsers.
trap: Returning borrowed slice tied to temp input dangles.

body_md: Async perf: pool connections (`deadpool`), batch with `buffered`, compress with `tower` layers. Monitor with `tokio-metrics`. Backpressure beats unbounded spawn.
code:
// let pool = deadpool_postgres::Pool::new(mgr, 16);
// let obj = pool.get().await.unwrap();
hook: 100k requests, 16 DB slots — pooling plus backpressure wins.

quiz.explain: Pools reuse connections, avoiding handshake cost.
quiz.q: How do you scale async DB access?

takeaway: Pool, batch, and bound async workloads.
trap: Unbounded spawn per request OOMs under burst.

body_md: Size matters: `cargo bloat --release` finds fat deps. Prefer `no_std` crates, `default-features = false`, `opt-level = "z"`. One heavy dep can double binary.
hook: Your hello-world is 2MB — here is exactly why.

quiz.explain: bloat ranks crates and symbols by size.
quiz.q: How do you find binary size culprits?

takeaway: Audit binary size; trim default features.
trap: Disabling features blindly breaks API; check docs.
